description: This bar chart, sourced from the paper “The Unseen Targets of Hate — A Systematic Review of Hateful Communication Datasets,” illustrates the number of datasets published per year from 2012 to 2022, categorized by the primary language of the dataset. The vertical axis, labeled “Number of datasets,” is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10² (100), with major gridlines at 1, 10, and 100. The horizontal axis represents the year, spanning 2012 to 2022. Each year features a grouped set of vertical bars, each corresponding to a language category as defined in the legend: “All other” (orange), “Arabic” (green), “Bengali” (red), “Spanish” (purple), “Russian” (brown), and an unlabeled gray bar (possibly representing a default or unspecified category, though its label is missing in the legend). The blue bar, labeled “Language” in the legend, appears to represent the total or a primary category across all years. Notably, the number of datasets grows over time, with a sharp increase from 2017 onward. In 2020 and 2021, the “All other” category (orange) and the blue “Language” bar reach their highest values, exceeding 50 datasets. Arabic, Spanish, and Russian datasets begin appearing around 2017–2018 and show moderate growth, while Bengali datasets remain sparse, with only a few instances. The 2022 data shows a decline in most categories except “All other,” which remains high. The chart visually emphasizes the dominance of non-specified or “All other” language datasets in recent years, alongside a growing but still limited representation of specific languages like Arabic and Spanish.
